parsed.why: Criminalised gender-expressive performance, birth-sex facility and indecent-exposure statutes, closed markers since 1977, no state nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage, documented violence and official indifference — a hostile layer above the parent's 0.35.

Placed in the low-risk tier: no facility, care or expression ban; anti-trans bills vetoed; state-employment nondiscrimination order; sodomy long repealed. Held below parent ceiling by the national passport/entry regime, missing statewide gender-identity protection and hate-crime gap.

Moderate-risk tier: no adult facility or care ban, but youth restrictions via appointed boards, a district birth-sex bathroom rule, no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination, and no gender identity in the hate-crime statute; documents available.

Most-protective tier: gender identity/expression covered in public accommodations, employment and housing, gender-identity hate-crime law with reporting unit, self-declared documents, shield law for care. Unenforced sodomy wording is tangential; national passport/entry regime caps the score.

Facility ban repealed but a 2025 bathroom bill revived; amended birth certificates must retain the original marker; no gender identity or sexual orientation in hate-crime law, only ~30% local ordinance coverage, youth-care and sports bans in force.
